# mabinogi-006 — review

## Pass 1 (units)

Reviewer pass 1 (2026-11-12). I read all 98 units and the "about" against conventions.md, packet.md (the established text and the establishment log), the published mabinogi-004 and 005, and drafts/mabinogi-005/review.md. Aids: Strachan, Morris-Jones, Silvan Evans and GPC, from knowledge. Third witness: Rhŷs & Evans 1905 (Red Book), `source/raw/rhys-evans1905_djvu.txt`, printed pp. 34–38. I checked every Red Book reading cited below on the page images (PDF pp. 48, 50–52). No English translation was consulted. Edits were made by a Python script (load, change fields by index, dump with ensure_ascii=False, indent=1). No `t` was touched. Afterwards I checked that there are 98 sentences and that every `t` equals cut.json.

**Unit numbers are 0-based.**

### Changes

- 77 · n · major · *yn braf* was glossed as 'stout, massive', said to be "left unsoftened after yn", and contrasted with modern *braf*. The Red Book writes *yn braff*. The word is *praff* 'thick, stout, massive', softened after predicative *yn* (p > b) like *yn uawr* beside it, with f for ff (as in *a fawb*). So the form is softened, and the lemma is not *braf*. · The note now says this, with the Red Book reading. l and i ("stout") stand.
- about · about · minor · It stopped at the hidden men in the bags. It left out Efnysien's killing of them, the englyn, and the peace and the conferring of the kingship on the boy, which end the part. · Two clauses added.
- 6 · l · minor · *ni rodei hi* was given in l as "(but) she-would-give", which drops the negative. The note glosses it 'that she did not give'. · "that-not she-would-give".
- 13 · n · minor · *y urodyr* was derived "← broder". The text's form is the plural *brodyr*. · "← brodyr".
- 15 · i · minor · "This was the vengeance they took:" puts *Sef* back into the English. The house drops it (005 review, units 35/53/85). · "The vengeance they took was to drive Branwen out … and make her bake … and have the butcher … come to her every day and box her ear."
- 27 · n · minor · The note read *pedeir degwlat a seithugeint* as 154 and did not say that the Red Book differs. The Red Book has *pedeir gwlat a seith ugeint*, with no *deg*, which gives 144. The softening of *gwlat* in *degwlat* was not mentioned. · Both added. The White Book's 154 is kept in l and i, and the note says the reckoning is not certain. The drafter's flag is answered: 154 is the right arithmetic for the White Book's words, but the witnesses disagree.
- 31 · i · minor · "These were the seven:" is a *Sef* rendering. · "The seven were Caradog son of Brân, …".
- 39 · n · minor · *henpych* was called "an old subjunctive of bot". It is the 2 sg. present subjunctive of *hanbot* (*hanfod*), a compound of *bot*. · Corrected, and the note now explains the sense of *guell* 'better' in the greeting. i "hail to you" stands.
- 43 · n · minor · *o pop parth* was explained only as "-p for -b". After *o* one expects *bop*, and unit 52 writes *o bop*. · The missing softening is noted.
- 50 · i, n · minor · *Och* was rendered "Ah" in i. 003 and 004 render it "Oh" in i (l keeps "Och"). · i "Oh". The note now reads "a cry of dismay (rendered as in the earlier parts)".
- 51 · n · minor · The drafter flagged the lemma. *kynghanei* was assigned to a verb "kynghanu". The verb is *genni* (MW also *gannu*) 'be contained, have room', with stem *gan-*/*gang-*. *kynghanei* is its compound with *kyn-* (gh for g as in *kynghor*). *enghis*, *ganho*, *ganhei* and 005's *angassei* belong to the simplex. · The note names *genni*, describes the compound, and gives the Red Book's *kyghanei*.
- 53 · n · minor · The note said *llynn* "was masculine a moment ago". Nothing earlier in the part shows its gender: *a'r llynn* would not show softening in any case. It also did not note the unsoftened *o pop parth*. · The note now says that *llynn* is usually masculine but is counted here with feminine *dwy* and softened (the Red Book agrees). The unsoftened *o pop* is noted (Red Book *o pob*).
- 55 · n · minor · The drafter flagged *y rot*. The note called it "a contracted form of rwng … the form is unusual". *y rot* is the regular 2 sg. of the conjugated *y rwng* (modern *rhyngot*), the counterpart of the house formula *y rof i a Duw*. It occurs already in the First Branch (*y rot a'th uarchogyon*, in the work glossary), and the Red Book has *yrot ac ef* here. · The note now says it is regular, with these parallels.
- 72 · n · minor · *enghis* was called the preterite "of angu". There is no such verb. The form is *genghis*, preterite of *genni*, softened after *Ni* with the g dropping away. · Corrected, with the Red Book's *nyt eigwys*.
- 73 · l, n · minor · *y ganho* was said to be "softened after y". *ganho* is the radical (*genni*), and the particle *y* causes no mutation. l also had "that may-hold him and the men", which makes *ef a gwyr* the object of an intransitive verb. They are its subject. · l "that may-fit he and the men". The note now says this, with the Red Book's *y geingho*. i ("to hold him and the men…") is acceptable English for the sense and stands.
- 79 · i · minor · "This was their trick:" is a *Sef* rendering. · "The trick they played was to set a peg …".
- 84 · n · minor · The drafter flagged *ureichell*. The note did not give the Red Book reading, which matters for a word glossed from context. On the page image it is *yny vreithell* (← *breithell*). · Added. 'brain' and *ymanodi* are still marked uncertain.
- 86 · n · minor · *medei* was called the imperfect "of medu 'say'". *medu* is 'possess'. *medei* belongs to the defective verb *meddaf* 'say', which has no verbal noun. · Corrected.
- 94 · l · minor · *kydwyr* was "battle-fellows" in l, which adds "battle". The note glosses it 'fellow-men, comrades' (*kyd-* + *gwyr*). · "before fellow-men battle-ready".
- 6 · n · style · The softening in *teyrndlws* (← *tlws*) was not mentioned. · Added.
- 7 · l · style · "that year she-it-was-that passed renownedly" garbled the abnormal sentence. It also rendered the same verb *duc* two ways ("passed", "had"). · "that year it-was-that she-bore renownedly, and a-comely course it-was-that she-bore of fame …".
- 11 · l · style · *y wyr* was "of men" in l, but the note glosses *y* as 'for' and i has "for men". · "best for men".
- 14 · l · style · *hyt nat* was "until" in l but 'so that not' in the note. · "so-that there-was-not".
- 17 · n · style · *na at*: the softening (*gat* → *at* after *na*) was not stated. · Added. The reading of *ua* stays uncertain, as the log requires.
- 33 · n · style · "plural because the subject is two" did not square with the singular *a drigwys* after the plural *Y seith hynny* in unit 32. · The note now says that after a subject placed first the verb is often singular, and here it is plural.
- 39 · l · style · *guell* was "well" in l, but the note glosses it 'better'. · "may-you-be better".
- 57 · n · style · The unsoftened *a torryssant* had no witness. · Added: the Red Book also has *ac a torrassant* (and *y pont*, also unsoftened). The drafter's claim is right: in this spelling a softened t is written d, so t here is unmutated.
- 66 · n · style · *aduyd* was "uncertain". The Red Book writes *atuyd*, the word for 'perhaps'. · Added. The note now gives 'and perhaps' firmly and leaves only the word's make-up uncertain.
- 68 · n · style · *ehegyr* had no witness. · Added: the Red Book has *yn ebrwyd* 'quickly'.
- 74 · n · style · The unsoftened *a tangnoueda* had no witness. · Added: the Red Book also has *a tangneuedha*. The drafter's claim is right.
- 79 · n · style · The unsoftened *o cant* had no witness. · Added: the Red Book has the same.
- 94 · n · style · The cause of the softening in *cad barawt* was not given, and the Red Book's *kytwyr* was not mentioned. · "softened after the feminine noun cad", and *kytwyr* added.

### Establishment-log items: all stated plainly
- Opening mid-line in col. 47, no initial (0). *e ymwlet* and the witness's *ymw[e]let* not adopted (6). *Guern uab* (10). *lonyd* with the asterisk dropped (14). Condensed line (17).
- *ua na at* (17): *ua* is certain on the image. The witness's *[ac]* and the Red Book's *hyt nat elont dracheuyn* are given, and the reading is said to be uncertain.
- *Dyuet dyuet* (31): dittography, kept, with the Red Book's reading. *Walltgrwn* as one word (31).
- *o gerd* raised (36). *dremynt* without *e* (38). *heb vy* (39). *a wnn* (47). *Nyt oed* (51). *y gwaelawt*, our division (56). *llynghes* (58). *kennedyf* and *hitheu* with h raised (59). *attat* (67). The blanks in col. 53 (72) and col. 54 (85). *Guydyl* (82). *a fawb* (87). *cad barawt* (94). *y'r ty*, *y'r mab* (95, 97).
- Nothing is supplied from the Red Book, and no note says otherwise.

### Drafter's flags, verified
- 4 *teir llong ar dec*: 'three on ten' = thirteen is right. Taking it in apposition to the plural verb is a reasonable account, and it is kept.
- 27: 154 for the White Book is right as arithmetic. The Red Book has 144. Now noted (above).
- 55 *y rot*: regular 2 sg. 'between you'. Corrected (above).
- 84 *ureichell* / *ymanodi*: both are correctly marked uncertain, and the Red Book's *vreithell* is added.
- 94 englyn: *kynniuyeit* (cf. *cynnif*) and *rac kydwyr* are correctly hedged. One l word was corrected (above).
- 17 *ua na at*: correctly hedged.
- 73–74 *anryded* / *enryded*: "rank" in l and i, which is the house rendering. *enryded* is said to be *anryded* with e.
- Names agree with 005: Efeydd Hir, Unig Glew Ysgwydd, Iddig son of Anarawg, Pendaran Dyfed (as in 004), Llasar. The other names are Edeirnion, Saith Marchog, Llinon and Gwern. *y Gwydyl* is "the Irish". *heb wy* is "said they" / "they said". *y wyrda* is "his noblemen". *Ynys y Kedyrn* is "the Island of the Mighty". *Duw a rodo da ywch* is "God give you good", as in 005. *Llyna* is "There-is".
- 53 *dwy lynn*: feminine counting, softened. The draft's wording was corrected (above).
- 57 and 74, *a torryssant* and *a tangnoueda*: genuinely unsoftened, since this orthography writes the softened t as d. The Red Book agrees.
- 77 *yn braf*: the claim was wrong. It is softened *praff* (above).
- 51, 72–74: the lemma is *genni* (*gannu*). Corrected (above).

### Refused
- **5, i "great rejoicing at their coming"**: *wrthunt* is 'towards them', and the note explains the welcome. The i is interpretive but fair. Kept.
- **20, *drydwen* 'starling'**: the note says that the identification with *drudwen* is not certain. Kept.
- **12, *wnathoedit* (no e)**: the spelling may be a slip for *wnaethoedit*, but it is not in the establishment log and I did not check it on the image. The note's grammar (pluperfect impersonal) is right. Not changed.
- **54, *uorbennyd* 'great chiefs'**: the note calls the word rare and its derivation tentative ("apparently"). Kept.
- **80, *orwyllt* "here softened"**: no false rule is asserted, and I can give no surer cause. Kept.
- **84, l "in the brain"**: l and i have to render the word somehow. The note marks it as taken from context and uncertain. Kept.
- **65, the force of *gossymdeitha Uatholwch***: the note already marks it uncertain. Kept.
- **72, i "No house has ever been able to hold him"**: this matches 005's rendering of *ny angassei*. Kept.

## Pass 2 (glossary)

I checked all 264 novel-form entries and the 29 under `__broaden__` against the text, the reviewed units and known-forms.json. Edits were made by a Python script in place, keeping indent=1. Afterwards the keys of gloss.json minus `__broaden__` were checked to equal novel-forms.json exactly (264). Every `__broaden__` value begins with its known entry verbatim (27 remain). units.json was re-read against the glossary, and four notes were brought into line (below). It still has 98 units with every `t` unchanged.

### Changes

- foen · gloss · major · The lemma was an invented "moen", with the meaning "uncertain" and the cause given as m > f after the article. The word is *poen* with the spirant after *y* 'her' (p > ph, written f), as unit 16's note says and as in *a fawb*. · Rewritten.
- ueis · gloss · major · The radical was "meis", with the meaning uncertain. The word is *beis* 'shallow water, ford', softened (b > u) after *y* 'to', as unit 33's note says. · Rewritten. No modern form is claimed.
- kynghanei, ganho, ganhei, enghis · gloss · major · The lemma was given as *cynnwys* (a different verb) for the first three. *enghis* was glossed "apparently 'went in, entered'; the lemma is unknown". All four belong to *genni* (MW also *gannu*) 'be contained, have room'. *kynghanei* is the compound with *kyn-*. *enghis* is *genghis*, softened after *Ni*. *ganho* and *ganhei* are radical after the particle *y*. In *y ganho ef a gwyr* the nouns are the subject. · All four rewritten as in pass 1, with the Red Book forms (*kyghanei*, *eigwys*, *geingho*, *geinghei*).
- doro · gloss · major · It was given as "dodi — to put". *doro* (= *dyro*) is the imperative of *rodi* 'give'. · Corrected.
- braf · gloss · major · It was given as "braf (braf) — fine, splendid". As decided in pass 1, the word is *praff* 'thick, stout', softened after predicative *yn*, with f for ff (Red Book *yn braff*). · Corrected.
- gossymdeitha · gloss · major · It was "3 sg. present/future … 'Matholwch will grant it'". The form is the 2 sg. imperative with *Uatholwch* as its object: 'provide for Matholwch'. · Corrected, in agreement with unit 65.
- kychwynnyssant · gloss · minor · The example "teir llong ar dec a gychwynnyssant" is not the text. · It now quotes the text: *y kychwynnyssant teir llong ar dec*.
- gael · gloss · minor · The cause was given as "after y 'to'". It is the possessive *y* 'its' (beichogi), as unit 8 says. · Corrected.
- somm · gloss · minor · It was "insult, affront … noun f., no modern form". The word is *som* (modern *siom*) 'deceit, trick'. · Corrected.
- diskynyssant · gloss · minor · "they went down / dispersed" contradicted unit 18's 'they settled'. · Corrected.
- delediw · gloss · minor · The lemma was "teledyw (no modern form)". GPC has *telediw*. · Corrected.
- drydwen · gloss · minor · The lemma was "trydwen", with a d-radical said to be possible. · Now *drudwen*, radical d-, with the identification still marked uncertain.
- degwlat · gloss · minor · It was glossed "a unit of ten lands (tens of cantrefs)". · Now *deg* + *gwlat* (softened in the compound), the probable 154, and the Red Book's 144, as in unit 27.
- dywyssogyon, benhaf · gloss · minor · The cause was given as *y* 'his, their' ("seven of his leaders"). It is *y* 'as' (and predicative *yn* for *yn benhaf*), as in units 29 and 32. *pennaf* was also given "no modern form", but *pennaf* is the modern form. · Corrected.
- fodor · gloss · minor · It was "Fodor … f- may be radical or mutated". The Red Book has *a ffodor*. The name is Ffodor, with F for ff (/f/), and ff does not change after *a*. · Corrected.
- 31 · n · minor · The note said "Ffodor, the spirant after a written F". The spirant mutation does not apply to ff. · Now "F written for ff … ff does not change after a (the Red Book a ffodor)".
- wlch · gloss · minor · It was "possibly soft-mutated Gwlch after a 'and'". *a* does not soften. · The softening claim is removed.
- phendaran · gloss · minor · It said "later Pryderi's guardian". He was already Pryderi's foster-father in the First Branch (004). · Corrected.
- edeirnon · gloss · minor · It called Edeirnion "the cantref in the north of Wales". It was a commote. · "a commote in north-east Wales".
- weithon · gloss · minor · It was given "no modern form", with the softening caused "after the imperative par". *weithon* (modern *weithian*) is always softened as an adverb. · Corrected.
- dremynt · gloss · minor · It was "soft-mutated after o achaws". *o achaws* causes no softening. The log and unit 38 say there is no visible cause, because Evans prints no *e*. · Corrected.
- henpych · gloss · minor · It was "(no modern form) — a greeting … meaning approximate". · Now *hanbot* (*hanfod*), the 2 sg. present subjunctive in *henpych guell* 'may you be better'.
- welewch · gloss · minor · It was "2 sg. present 'you see'". It is the 2 pl. imperfect, as unit 42 says. · Corrected.
- welat · gloss · minor · It was "impersonal imperfect". It is the impersonal preterite in -at, as unit 48 says (*welit* is the imperfect). · Corrected.
- gwelem · gloss · minor · It was "imperfect/preterite … form uncertain". · Now the 1 pl. imperfect, which is certain.
- kedyrn · gloss · minor · The lemma was "cedyrn (cedyrn)". · Now *cadarn*, with the plural used as a noun.
- codyant · gloss · minor · It was "offence, outrage (cf. codi 'to rise')", which is the wrong *codi*. · Now *codiant* 'affliction, hurt' (cf. MW *codi* 'hurt, vex'), as in unit 64.
- aduyd · gloss · minor · It was "probably 'then, afterwards' or 'perhaps'". · Now 'perhaps', with the Red Book's *atuyd*, as in unit 66.
- deimlaw · gloss · minor · It was "after y 'it' … 'to feel it'". It is *y* 'his' (feeling him), as unit 84 says. · Corrected.
- glyw · gloss · minor · It was "3 sg. present subjunctive". *clyw* is the present indicative, here a vivid present. · Corrected.
- keimeit · gloss · minor · It was "warriors, champions, strides (cf. ceim 'step')". · Now *keimyat* (*ceimiad*) 'champion'.
- kynniuyeit · gloss · minor · It was "gatherers … (cf. cynnull)". This contradicted unit 94. · Now *kynniuyat* (*cynnifiad*) 'warrior' (cf. *cynnif*), and still uncertain.
- dothyw · gloss · minor · It was "3 sg. preterite … unusual form in -yw, uncertain". · Now the old 3 sg. perfect, as unit 95 says.
- duundeb · gloss · minor · It was "undeb … the du- prefix is unclear". GPC has *duundeb* (from *duun* 'agreed'). · Corrected.
- uorbennyd · gloss · minor · It was "mor 'sea' + penn … sea-captains". This contradicted unit 54 ('great chiefs', *mawr* + *penn*). · Both now give 'great chiefs' first and mention *mor* + *penn*, and both say the word is uncertain.
- drwydi · gloss · minor · It claimed "soft-mutated (t>d) after the verbal noun uynet". MW writes *drwy* where no mutation is due (*drwy Linon*). · Corrected.
- rot (broaden) · gloss · minor · The broadening glossed *y rot ac ef* as "between (it) and him … between them and him". It is 'between you and him', which the known entry already covers. · Removed.
- dal (broaden) · gloss · minor · The cause was given as "soft after y 'the'". In *ar dal y noe* the softening is after *ar*. · Corrected.
- ys (broaden) · gloss · minor · It was "'then I shall take', a preverbal particle (a variant of yd)". This contradicted *aduyd* 'perhaps'. · Now: perhaps the particle, perhaps the infixed 's 'it', uncertain, with the Red Book's *atuyd ys kymeraf*.
- teyrndlws · gloss · style · It said "no mutation". · *tlws* softened to *dlws* in the compound.
- amseroyd · gloss · style · It said "after the article y'r". The text has *yr*. · Corrected.
- lliwaw · gloss · style · It said "meaning uncertain here". 'Reproach' is the established sense, as in unit 13. · Firmed.
- cauas · gloss · style · It said "where he found". The subject is the bird. · "where it [the bird] found".
- dadleu · gloss · style · It said "in debate for himself, in council". · "holding court".
- their · gloss · style · The lemma was "tair (tair)". · "teir (tair)".
- kynueissat, kynweisyat · gloss · style · They said "no modern form". · *cynweisiad*, as in unit 32.
- arwest · gloss · style · It said "music, minstrelsy". · "string (of an instrument)", uncertain, as in unit 36.
- wchi · gloss · style · It said "probably transposed from chwi". · "a variant spelling of the pronoun".
- hwylbrenni · gloss · style · The softening p > b in the compound was not named. · Added.
- torryssant, tangnoueda, cant · gloss · style · The missing softening was not stated. · Stated, with the Red Book agreeing in each case.
- ehegyr · gloss · style · · The Red Book's *yn ebrwyd* added.
- racdu · gloss · style · It said "no modern form". · *rhagddo*.
- gwra · gloss · style · It said "the lemma is a guess". *gwrhau* is the GPC verb. · Corrected.
- ystynnu, ystynnwyt · gloss · style · The example "handing it to your keeping" did not match unit 64 ("in your presence"). · Aligned. The modern form is now *estyn*.
- draws · gloss · style · It said "on his back". · Removed.
- efnyssyen · gloss · style · The modern form was "Efnisien", but the units use Efnysien. · Efnysien.
- ymanodi, ureichell · gloss · style · They said "work, move, probe about", and the Red Book reading was missing. · Aligned with unit 84, and *vreithell* added.
- ban, benn, uatholwch (broaden) · gloss · style · The *ban* example misquoted the text. *am benn* (unit 91) and the object *Uatholwch* (unit 65) were not covered. · Fixed and added.
- gouyn (broaden) · gloss · style · The broadening was not needed: the known entry already covers the verbal noun. · Removed.
- 39 · n · style · The note said "'may you be well'", against l "may-you-be better". · "'may you be better'".
- 42 · n · style · *wchi* was called "the emphatic form" of *chwi*. · "a spelling of chwi, the pronoun repeated after the verb".
- 54 · n · style · · Aligned with the glossary on *uorbennyd*, as above.

### Refused
- **beis**: no modern form is given ("no common modern form"). I was not sure enough of a GPC headword to name one.
- **medei**: the glossary already gives the defective verb (*meddai*), in agreement with pass 1. Kept.
- **orwyllt**: it says "cause unclear", as unit 80 does. Kept.
- The remaining broadenings (wr, gwyr, kyn, uendigeiduran, uranwen, wyd, down, hyn, lu, law, was, barawt, yscwyd, edewit, lynn, llynn, ryw, ay, uu, ueirch, uawr, gerdet) are each needed and correct. Kept.
